top_papers.title: Context Cache: Efficient Long-Context Inference with Semantic-Aware Prompt Compression
top_papers.abstract: Long-context language models can process up to 1M tokens, but the quadratic cost of attention makes practical deployment expensive. We introduce Context Cache, a semantic-aware prompt compression system that caches and reuses compressed representations across similar queries. Unlike naive token-level pruning, Context Cache operates at the semantic chunk level: it partitions prompts into coherent segments, computes semantic embeddings, and identifies reusable blocks that appear across multiple queries (e.g., system prompts, shared context, retrieved documents). On a benchmark of multi-turn RAG tasks with shared document sets, Context Cache achieves 2.7x latency reduction and 60% KV-cache memory savings while preserving 97% of task accuracy. The system integrates with vLLM and SGLang serving backends with minimal code changes, making it immediately deployable in production RAG pipelines.

top_papers.title: AgentSandbox: A Reproducible and Scalable Evaluation Platform for LLM-based Agents
top_papers.abstract: Evaluating LLM-based agents is challenging due to non-deterministic behavior, external API dependencies, and lack of reproducibility. We present AgentSandbox, an open-source evaluation platform that provides fully deterministic, reproducible environments for agent testing. Key innovations include: (1) hermetic containers that mock all external dependencies (file system, network, APIs) with record-replay capabilities, (2) a protocol for defining evaluation tasks as stateful environments with clear success criteria, and (3) a scoring framework that separates reasoning quality from execution correctness. AgentSandbox ships with 200 evaluation tasks across 5 domains (coding, data analysis, web browsing, system administration, multi-tool orchestration). We benchmark 12 frontier models and find that agent capabilities vary dramatically across domains: GPT-4.1 excels at coding (82% success) but struggles with system administration (34%), while Claude 3.5 shows more balanced performance (68%/61%). All experiments are one-click reproducible.

top_papers.title: Safety Rigor via Red Teaming Games: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Adversarial LLM Safety Evaluation
top_papers.abstract: Current LLM safety evaluations treat red teaming as a fixed benchmark, which fails to capture the adversarial and adaptive nature of real-world threats. We formalize LLM safety evaluation as a Red Teaming Game (RTG), a two-player zero-sum game between an attacker and a defender. The attacker generates adversarial prompts to elicit unsafe outputs, while the defender adapts safety training and guardrail configurations. We prove that under mild assumptions, the game has a unique mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium that provides rigorous safety guarantees. Empirically, we instantiate RTG with 12 attack strategies and 8 defense configurations across 6 safety categories. The equilibrium analysis reveals that current production LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 2.0) are significantly more vulnerable than static benchmarks suggest: equilibrium attack success rates are 2.3x higher than the best single-attack baseline. Our framework provides a principled way to benchmark safety under adversarial pressure.

top_papers.title: Chain-of-Specification: Bridging Natural Language Requirements to Formal Verification with LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: We introduce Chain-of-Specification (CoSpec), a framework that uses LLM agents to automatically translate natural language requirements into formal specifications for system verification. The core challenge is bridging the gap between informal human-readable requirements and precise formal languages like TLA+, Alloy, and SMT-LIB. CoSpec employs a multi-agent pipeline: a Parser Agent extracts structured requirements, a Specification Agent generates formal code, and a Verification Agent validates the output against test cases and counterexamples. On a benchmark of 500 real-world system requirements, CoSpec achieves 72% end-to-end translation accuracy, significantly outperforming single-pass prompting (38%) and retrieval-augmented baselines (51%). The framework also identifies ambiguous or contradictory requirements that are common in large-scale system design. We demonstrate practical integration with existing model checking workflows, reducing human specification effort by an estimated 60%.
top_papers.llm_reason: CoSpec 将 LLM Agent 多步推理应用于形式化规约翻译，直接打通自然语言需求到 TLA+/Alloy/SMT-LIB 的工程链路。72% 端到端准确率 + 减少 60% 人工规约工作量，工程价值明确。多 Agent 流水线（Parser→Spec→Verify）是可复用的架构模式，可迁移到合同审查、合规检查等场景。缺少开源代码是主要风险。

top_papers.title: Speculative Retrieval: Overlapping Retrieval and Generation for Low-Latency RAG Systems
top_papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems suffer from latency overhead because retrieval and generation are executed sequentially. We propose Speculative Retrieval, a technique that overlaps retrieval and generation by predicting future information needs based on the current generation context. A lightweight predictor model, trained on retrieval logs, anticipates which documents will be needed for upcoming tokens and pre-fetches them speculatively. When the prediction is correct, retrieval latency is effectively hidden behind generation. On standard RAG benchmarks (NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA, MS MARCO), Speculative Retrieval reduces end-to-end latency by 40-55% with negligible impact on answer quality (less than 1% F1 drop). The predictor achieves 78% top-5 recall for future retrieval needs, and mispredictions are safely handled by falling back to synchronous retrieval. The system is compatible with any embedding-based retriever and transformer-based generator.

top_papers.title: Adaptive Tool Composition for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning with Offline Bases
top_papers.abstract: Tool-augmented LLM agents achieve remarkable performance on complex tasks, but current approaches rely on static tool sets and hand-crafted composition strategies that fail to adapt to novel task distributions. We propose ATCO, an Adaptive Tool Composition framework that uses reinforcement learning to learn dynamic tool selection and composition policies. ATCO pre-trains on offline tool-use trajectories from existing benchmarks (ToolBench, APIBank, ToolAlpaca) and fine-tunes with online RL to discover novel tool combinations. On a suite of 8 held-out tasks requiring multi-step tool composition, ATCO improves task completion rates by 18% over the strongest baseline (ToolLLaMA) while reducing average tool calls by 30%. Ablation studies reveal that the RL component is critical for generalizing to unseen tool combinations, while the offline base prevents reward hacking during online exploration.

top_papers.title: MemoryPalace: A Structured Memory Architecture for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents
top_papers.abstract: Embodied agents operating in complex 3D environments over extended time horizons need to maintain and query spatial-temporal memory efficiently. We introduce MemoryPalace, a structured memory architecture inspired by the classical mnemonic technique. MemoryPalace organizes agent experiences into a hierarchical spatial graph: rooms contain objects with temporal state histories, and cross-room relationships capture navigational affordances. Unlike unstructured conversation-based memory, MemoryPalace supports efficient queries like 'where did I last see the red cup?' or 'what changed in the kitchen since I was last here?' in O(log n) time. On the Habitat 2.0 benchmark for long-horizon household tasks, MemoryPalace improves task success rates by 24% over the best baseline (ConceptGraphs) while reducing memory usage by 45%. The architecture is model-agnostic and can wrap any base LLM/VLM planner.

top_papers.title: MultiHop-R1: Incentivizing Multi-Hop Reasoning in Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: Large reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 have shown strong single-chain reasoning capabilities, but they struggle with multi-hop reasoning that requires connecting information across multiple documents or knowledge domains. We present MultiHop-R1, a reinforcement learning framework that specifically incentivizes multi-hop reasoning behaviors in language models. We design a reward function that decomposes multi-hop tasks into intermediate reasoning milestones and provides dense rewards for correct information bridging. Training with GRPO on a curated dataset of 15K multi-hop question-answer pairs, MultiHop-R1-7B outperforms DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B by 12.3% on MuSiQue and 8.7% on 2WikiMultiHopQA, while using 40% fewer reasoning tokens. Analysis reveals that the model learns to explicitly plan retrieval steps and cross-reference information before answering, rather than guessing from partial evidence.

top_papers.title: Distilling Reasoning Trace via Knowledge Gap Alignment for Smaller Language Models
top_papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation from large reasoning models to smaller ones often fails because the teacher's reasoning traces contain knowledge gaps that the student cannot bridge. We propose Knowledge Gap Alignment (KGA), a distillation method that identifies and fills these gaps before transferring reasoning traces. KGA first probes the student model on each step of the teacher's reasoning chain to detect comprehension failures, then generates bridging explanations at those points. The augmented traces are used for supervised fine-tuning, followed by a reinforcement learning phase where the student learns to generate its own gap-filling reasoning. Experiments show that KGA-distilled Qwen2.5-7B matches the reasoning quality of Qwen2.5-32B on MATH (93.2% vs 93.8%) and GPQA (71.4% vs 72.1%) while being 4.5x faster at inference. The method is particularly effective for multi-step mathematical and scientific reasoning tasks.
